targetCompanyImage.name: PurposeEnergy
targetCompanyImage.description: PurposeEnergy develops, owns and operates organics-to-energy infrastructure that converts food and beverage residuals and wastewater into biogas, renewable electricity, renewable natural gas, clean water and related by-products. Quinbrook announced its acquisition of the platform on April 12, 2023 through its Net Zero Power Fund strategy; a separate legal closing date, exact stake and holding vehicle were not publicly disclosed. PurposeEnergy's project portfolio includes Middlebury Resource Recovery Center in Vermont, which reached commercial operation on October 21, 2024; the Minster, Ohio industrial-biogas facility, which began taking waste on July 16, 2026 and remained in ramp-up; and the operating South Burlington, Vermont brewery-waste digester historically associated with Magic Hat and now Zero Gravity. These facility and SPV names are project identities beneath PurposeEnergy and are not separate manager-level portfolio companies. No later PurposeEnergy equity transfer or signed pending sale was identified through September 1, 2026.

milestones.event: PurposeEnergy broke ground on the Middlebury Resource Recovery Center in Vermont.
Public sources identify PurposeEnergy's founding year as 2007.
Quinbrook said the acquisition marked its move into renewable fuels infrastructure.
Quinbrook announced its acquisition of PurposeEnergy through its renewable-fuels strategy; a separate legal closing date was not publicly disclosed.
PurposeEnergy's 1.014 MW Middlebury facility reached commercial operation in Vermont.
PurposeEnergy opened its St. Albans, Vermont facility.
PurposeEnergy reported that its Minster, Ohio facility had begun taking waste and would ramp over the following months; full commercial operation was not yet confirmed.
Magic Hat and Purpose Energy executed the development agreement for the South Burlington brewery digester project.

PurposeEnergy reports the South Burlington digester was commissioned in 2009; historical reporting places construction completion in July 2010 and restart in June 2011, so no false exact operating date is asserted.
